public_rationale: Business Insider and The Next Web report that Uber's CTO told The Information in April 2026 that Uber had used up its entire planned 2026 AI coding budget in four months. In a podcast released May 23, 2026, COO Andrew Macdonald said higher token use was not producing a matching rise in useful features, and that the link 'is not there yet.' Both parts of Marcus's sentence match these reports. One nuance: the budget was for AI coding tools such as Claude Code, which are paid for by tokens, not necessarily all of Uber's AI spending.
limitations: The facts rest on news reports of executive statements, not on Uber filings.
Marcus's 'token budget' slightly simplifies the reported 'AI coding budget.'

our_interpretation: Plain reading: by the time of the post, Uber had used up its planned 2026 budget for AI tokens or AI coding tools within the first few months of 2026, and a senior Uber executive had said publicly that the spending was not producing the expected productivity gains.
An Uber AI coding-tool budget (for example Claude Code), which is paid for by token use, counts as the 'token budget'.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reports that an Uber executive said the company had used up its 2026 AI budget within a few months, and that an Uber executive said the productivity gains do not match the rising AI costs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Uber had not used up its annual AI budget early, or Uber executives said the AI spending was paying off as hoped.
